read.passage: Saudi Arabia produces more desalinated water than any other country, and much of the drinking water in its cities comes from the sea. Desalination, however, uses a great deal of energy, so experts urge people to treat water as a valuable resource. It is estimated that a dripping tap can waste thousands of litres a year, yet many families never think about such small leaks. Some people argue that one household saving water is just a drop in the ocean. Researchers point out, though, that small changes add up when millions of people make them. Shorter showers, fixing leaks and running the washing machine only when it is full are simple steps. Newer desalination plants are also using solar power, which could make the process cleaner in the future.

qs.q: Why do experts want people to save water?
options: Because desalination uses a lot of energy
Because there is no sea nearby
qs.cando: Can understand articles on social and scientific topics.

qs.q: What do some people argue about one household saving water?
qs.cando: Can understand articles on social and scientific topics.

options: Small changes add up across millions of people.
qs.cando: Can understand articles on social and scientific topics.
Can understand articles on social and scientific topics.

read2.passage: Falconry has been practised in Arabia for thousands of years, and it is now recognised by UNESCO as part of humanity's living heritage. Yet only a few decades ago, the tradition was thought to be in decline, as fewer young people were willing to spend the long hours that training a falcon requires. Today, the picture looks rather different. Falconry clubs report rising membership among teenagers, many of whom are drawn in by competitions broadcast online. Conservationists have welcomed this renewed interest, provided that birds are bred in captivity rather than taken from the wild. According to one breeder, the hardest lesson for beginners is patience: 'A falcon will not be rushed. It is said that it takes a year to train a bird and a lifetime to understand one.'

qs.q: Why was falconry thought to be in decline?
options: Young people were unwilling to spend the time.
qs.cando: Can understand articles on social and scientific topics.

qs.q: What has attracted teenagers to falconry?

options: Birds should be released after a year.
Birds should be bred in captivity.
